title: Seeing the Unseen in Micro-Video Popularity Prediction: Self-Correlation Retrieval for Missing Modality Generation

problem.claim: Micro-video popularity prediction is important for applications such as product marketing and recommendation systems.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal learning methods predominantly assume complete modalities, but practical constraints can cause modalities to be missing.

contributions.claim: SCRAG is a retrieval-augmented generative framework for improving missing-modality robustness in micro-video popularity prediction.
SCRAG combines a self-correlation retriever with a multimodal mixture-of-experts generator in a retrieval-guided generation process.
SCRAG uses multimodal prompt alignment to retrieve relevant instances and extracts contextual modal information from those instances for missing-content reconstruction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe SCRAG as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three real-world datasets reportedly show that SCRAG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report that SCRAG improves the accuracy of micro-video popularity prediction while handling incomplete modalities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Micro-video popularity prediction supports several real-world applications.
Complete-modality assumptions in existing multimodal methods often fail under practical constraints.
The paper proposes SCRAG to improve robustness to missing modalities.
SCRAG retrieves relevant instances, extracts contextual modal information, and learns joint modality distributions to reconstruct missing content.
The authors report consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across three real-world datasets.
